dedupe_keys.name: uk future of tv distribution evidence stakeholder forum papers ofcom report and 2026 green paper

description: This body of UK planning evidence addresses whether and when digital terrestrial television (DTT, branded Freeview) should be switched off in favour of internet delivery. On 23 June 2026 the Department for Culture, Media and Sport published sixteen papers from its Future of TV Distribution Stakeholder Forum, on infrastructure (a reduced nightlight DTT service, environmental impact, IPTV readiness), audiences (internet access and speeds, universality, impacts), television economics and carriage, with annexes on international context and technology. The Freeview 2034 to 2044 paper reports that in 2025 about 13 million households had DTT access and 2.9 million (9 per cent) relied on it alone, with homes without connected TV projected to fall from 2.3 million in 2030 to 1.5 million in 2040; it sets out Arqiva's proposal for a three-multiplex DVB-T2 platform from 2035 that would cut annual transmission charges from about 231 to 139 million pounds, clear the 600 MHz band and use 40 per cent less energy. The same day DCMS opened the Watch this space green paper consultation (to 31 August 2026), which press reports say weighs switch-off in 2034 or 2044. Ofcom's 2024 Future of TV Distribution report is the regulator's input. Coverage: United Kingdom, projections to 2044. Format and access: HTML and PDF papers on GOV.UK, free under the Open Government Licence. Caveats: the forum papers are stakeholder views, not DCMS policy; figures are disputed between broadcasters and Arqiva. Simulation uses: scenarios for retiring a broadcast network, capacity planning of broadband to replace it, and equity effects on older, low-income and disabled households. Related records: the LoCaT studies give energy per viewing hour by platform.
